LESSON: TRANSPORT IN PLANTS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Life Science
Topic 1.4: Transport in plants
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Transport in plants, part of Life Science in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: Why is transport in plants important? 2. How do plants absorb water and mineral salts?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss and use digital devices or print media to search for information on absorption of water and mineral salts in plants and present their findings. Learners with speech difficulties could use Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application/ point/sign/write) to express their views. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted digital resources to conduct research. Regulate 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss and use digital devices or print media to search for information on absorption of water and mineral salts in plants and present their findings. Learners with speech difficulties could use Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application/ point/sign/write) to express their views. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted digital resources to conduct research. Regulate 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Transport in plants together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: as the learner sensitises the community on the importance of watering and manuring plants to sustain plant

growth.

● Learning to learn: as the learner reflects on experiments on factors affecting transpiration in plants.

Values:
● Unity: as the learner engages in assigned roles while working with others in the process of investigation of factors

affecting transpiration.

● Patriotism: as the learner sensitises the community on the importance of watering and manuring plants to sustain plant

growth.

● Safety and security: as the learner observes safety precautions as they carry out experiments in groups to investigate

factors affecting transpiration in plants.

● Environmental issues: as the learner creates awareness in the community on the use of fertilisers (Di-ammonium

phosphate, Calcium Ammonium Nitrate, Urea) in boosting crop production.

Text books, Plant specimens (Fresh stalks with leaves), Food colouring (red or blue), Local environment, Plastic bags,
